text:
kai: Heads up — planning a maintenance window for apac-saturn-edge cluster (saturn-2) tomorrow 02:00–05:00 UTC. We'll run NIC firmware flip + rolling node drains. Expect ~10–12% GPU capacity dip during peak of the window.

maggie: ETA on KV-cache thaw/warmup? Any customer-facing impact to Hosted API?

zain: For Hosted API we’ll route >=P1 traffic to eu/us fallback region via smart-routing policy; Dedicated pools for commitments will stay pinned to local racks but we'll only drain non-critical cohorts first. Should be minimal 95th percentile change.

liam: KV-cache plan: seed 4 warm nodes before bulk drain, then incremental kvcache re-seed. Quick snippet for the drain runbook:

```
# drain sequence (run on control plane)
kubectl cordon node-saturn-02-0${i}
kubectl drain node-saturn-02-0${i} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# then trigger kvseed job
kubectl create job kvseed-primers --from=cronjob/kvseed --namespace infra
```

kai: Nice. We'll do a 10-min canary on 2 nodes first, confirm cache hit-rate, then continue. Ops-bot, please schedule rolling drain job at 02:10 UTC after canary approval.

ops-bot: Scheduled rolling-drain-job for apac-saturn-edge at 2026-03-22T02:10:00Z. Canary nodes: node-saturn-02-01,node-saturn-02-02.

oncall: FYI oncall will be watching latency dashboards and token error rate during the window. Ping us with any >=2x P50 increase.

maggie: What about spot-backed capacity cost impact? If we lose 12% capacity, burst to other regions will incur egress and cross-region costs. Estimate ~ $1.2k – $2.5k for the 3h window depending on burst level. Recommend enabling transient-burst quota to contain unexpected spill.

zain: Agreed — enable quota + set routing to prefer same-region cheap model variants first. Also add a failback policy to route low-priority jobs to cheaper quantized variants to avoid price spikes.

liam: I'll update the runbook with the rollback steps and netpol sync commands. Netpol change: flip egress-allow for scheduler namespace, then revert after drains. Example:

```
# apply netpol sync
kubectl apply -f netpol-egress-allow-scheduler.yaml --namespace=scheduler
# revert after window
kubectl delete -f netpol-egress-allow-scheduler.yaml --namespace=scheduler
```

kai: Communication plan: status page banner 01:30 UTC, customer email to affected Dedicated accounts 01:40 UTC, and in-console notice for model infra routes. I'll draft the blurb.

maggie: Add a line to the email about expected degraded throughput for non-critical batch jobs and that real-time endpoints should be unaffected for most customers.

zain: Can we get two volunteers to monitor kv-hit rates and egress counters during canary? @liam @kai?

liam: I'll take kv-hit rates. Kai will watch egress and routing failovers.

kai: I'll also post short updates in #incidents during the window. If we see >3% sustained 5m error rise we abort and rollback.

maggie: Thumbs up. Please update the RFC doc with final schedule + cost estimate after you schedule the run. :thumbsup:

liam: One last note — keep an eye on multi-tenant tenants with pinned GPUs (tenant-42, tenant-88) — we'll exclude them from canary and coordinate maintenance with their PMs.

kai: Will do. Summary: 02:00–05:00 UTC, canary 02:10, expected ~10–12% capacity dip, KV cache seed + netpol sync, cost hedge via quotas + cheaper model variants, status page/email at 01:30/01:40. Thanks all — any last call?

zain: No objections. Good to go on my side. :white_check_mark:
